newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: South Port hit by depressed rural sector.
newsitem.headline: South Port hit by depressed rural sector.

text.p: South Port Group confirmed earlier projections of a lower tax paid profit result of NZ$3.5 million for the year to June 30 but was increasing dividend payout for the third consecutive year, said chairman Rex Powley on Friday.
South Port Group profit declined 24.7 percent from 1995 tax paid profit of NZ$4.6 million.

Rural sector earnings were cyclical and there were reduced earnings from a depressed rural sector, reflecting the flow-on effect of adverse international commodity prices and bad debt write offs, said Powley.
Rural sector profit contribution was down more than NZ$1 million on 1995 levels.
South Port's directors had previously stated their objective to reduce the Group's exposure to the rural sector.

However, record trade volumes through the Port of Bluff have stabilised the overall reduction. Steps taken to position the port-owning parent company for future growth have begun to make a positive contribution, and in the latest year approximately 70 percent of profit was generated by the port activity.
Cargo tonnage of 1,770,151 tonnes set a record for the second consecutive year.

"The parent company's tax paid earnings were ahead 4 percent at NZ$2.5 million after allowing for additional funding and depreciation costs associated with significant fixed asset purchases such as a NZ$5.5 million Liebherr mobile harbour crane" said Powley.
Total assets were NZ$71.1 million at June 30 and return on operating assets was 10.7 percent.
Directors recommended a final dividend of 4 cents per share, taking the total annual dividend payment to 6.25 cents per share. -- Wellington Newsroom 64 4 4734746
